## NORTH MACEDONIA — profile (page 202)

- Header facts: Region: Europe & Central Asia; income group: Upper-middle-income; lending category: IBRD; data status: Data as reported (A); population: 1.8 million; GNI: 18,183; unit line: US$ million, unless otherwise indicated.
- Total external debt stock 2025: 14,332; change from 2024: +12.6%.

- Figure 1 Total external debt, 2015–25: 6,592 (2015) to 14,332 (2025). The line rises overall across the period, with modest increases through the late 2010s, stronger gains after ≈2020, and the highest point in 2025.

- Figure 2 External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations:
  - Total external debt: 14,332
  - Public & publicly guaranteed: 6,730
  - Private nonguaranteed: 3,864
  - Short-term: 3,739

  - Public & publicly guaranteed — by creditor type:
    - Multilateral: 2,563
    - Bilateral: 1,931
    - Private creditors: 2,236

  - Multilateral:
    - World Bank-IBRD: 718
    - EBRD: 401
    - Other multilateral: 1,444

  - Bilateral:
    - Hungary: 1,175
    - China: 441
    - Other bilateral: 315

- Figure 3 Debt ratios, 2015–25:
  - External debt / exports: 123%; change: +3.1%. Trend: low and fairly flat through most of the period, dipping around the middle years and edging up by 2025.
  - External debt / GNI: 79%; change: -0.4%. Trend: rises from 2015 to a peak around ≈2020, then eases slightly and is broadly stable by 2025.
  - Debt service / exports: 20%; change: +41.0%. Trend: volatile, falling in the first half of the period, then fluctuating and ending on an upswing in 2025.
  - Debt service / GNI: 13%; change: +36.1%. Trend: volatile with several swings, but generally rising toward a peak in 2025.

- Figure 4 Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025:
  - Official creditors: maturity 16 yrs; grace period 4 yrs; interest rate 3.0%.
  - Private creditors: maturity ..; grace period ..; interest rate ...

- Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
- Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
